id: AJC.albanese.symmetric
title: Abel-Jacobi and symmetric-power factorisation
projects:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
summary: "Abel-Jacobi and symmetric-power factorisation.\n\nSTATE (run 0069 r4). Milne's\
  \ ARGUMENT is proved; the missing thing is one object.\n\nPROVED, sorry-free and\
  \ axiom-clean, over the symmetric power as an INTERFACE:\n * SymPowInterface.lean\
  \  -- SymPowData C n; symAVMap (Milne's Sym^n phi) as a\n   CONSTRUCTION; basePointShift_comp_powSum\
  \ (the \"use phi(P0)=eta_A\" collapse).\n * AlbaneseFromData.lean -- the connector\
  \ in BOTH directions and Milne III.6.1\n   assembled; exists_unique_descent_of_birational\
  \ is Milne's step 2 in full.\n * SymPowColimit.lean    -- the pair (D, hproj) IS\
  \ a colimit of the S_n-action on\n   C^n, in both directions (hasColimit_permDiagram_iff),\
  \ so the reduction is\n   LOSSLESS; hproj is colimit.w, free at every n.\n * AlbaneseFromColimit.lean\
  \ -- the same capstone with no SymPowData argument.\n\nTHE CARRIER IS NOW NAMED\
  \ (this round, SymPowInvariants.lean). SymPowColimit had\nflagged three times that\
  \ the affine quotient was inhabited but NOT identified.\nfixedConeIsLimit: the invariant\
  \ subring A^G IS the limit of the SingleObj G action\ndiagram in CommRingCat; fixedCoconeIsColimitOp\
  \ dualises it into CommRingCat^op,\nthe variance the interface consumes. No finiteness\
  \ on G and no Noetherian\nhypothesis -- finiteness is what the GEOMETRY of Spec\
  \ A -> Spec A^G needs\n(integrality, surjectivity), not the universal property.\
  \ This matters because\ngluing compares two overlapping charts' quotients, and a\
  \ comparison needs a\nformula per side: an abstract colimit supplies none, A^G does.\n\
  \nONE GLUING INPUT LANDED (SymPowInvariantsLocalization.lean): the action transports\n\
  to a localization at an invariant element (awayMap), and an invariant element of\n\
  A_b has an INVARIANT NUMERATOR (exists_invariant_numerator) -- the substantive\n\
  half of (A_b)^G = (A^G)_b, which mathlib lacks. Characteristic-free: no averaging\n\
  over G, since |G| = g! may vanish in A. Finiteness is spent only on a max of\nexponents;\
  \ invariance of b is what makes b^m*a invariant.\n\nOPEN, and this is the whole\
  \ residue of the leg: HasColimit (permDiagram C g) for\nthe curve -- i.e. the GLUING\
  \ of the affine quotients into a scheme. State it\nper-diagram, NEVER as HasColimitsOfShape\
  \ (SingleObj (Perm (Fin g))) Scheme: the\nquantified form is strictly stronger and\
  \ believed false at this pin (schemes have\nno coequalizers), so a theorem carrying\
  \ it would be vacuous. Availability measured:\nHasCoproducts Scheme YES, HasCoequalizers/HasPushouts\
  \ NO, Scheme.GlueData YES.\nRemaining work is the cocycle/overlap compatibility\
  \ of the chart quotients.\n\nNOT the residue, and not this node's debt: abelJacobi.\
  \ It is blocked on a\nDIFFERENT and earlier brick -- the line bundle O(Delta - {P0}xC\
  \ - Cx{P0}) on CxC\nis nowhere constructed in the tree, and there is no in-tree\
  \ producer of any\nDivFamily to feed PicScheme.abelMap. Measured this round. The\
  \ 2400-3800 line\nfigure in analogies/m3-route-audit.md is HISTORICAL; read SymPowColimit.lean\
  \ and\nSymPowInvariants.lean before budgeting from it.\n"

summary: "Albanese universal property. THE ARGUMENT IS NOW PROVED (run 0069, session\
  \ 0004); what remains is one missing OBJECT.\n\nMILNE III.6.1 IS PROVED, both connector\
  \ directions, over the symmetric power taken as an interface rather than a sorry\
  \ -- Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean and Albanese/AlbaneseJacobian.lean, sorry-free.\
  \ Forward (symAVMap_eq_of_albanese_eq) needs psi to be a HOMOMORPHISM: pushing psi\
  \ through the g-fold sum is map_prod (IsMonHom.monoidHom), which is exactly where\
  \ Milne's step 5 uses homomorphy. Backward (albanese_eq_of_symAVMap_eq) needs NEITHER\
  \ that nor the quotient universal property -- it is restriction along Q |-> (Q,P0,...,P0)\
  \ plus the collapse basePointShift_comp_powSum. The pinned docstring described both\
  \ as one step; they are not the same difficulty.\n\nMilne's identification of the\
  \ Abel-Jacobi map with 'Q |-> Q + (g-1)P0 followed by f^(g)' is DERIVED (basePointShift_proj_comp),\
  \ not assumed; and pointed rigidity is applied only after PROVING the candidate\
  \ psi is pointed.\n\nTHE MEASUREMENT, which attributes the residual sorry rather\
  \ than asserting whose it is:\n    #print axioms albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData_generic\
  \ -> [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]  AXIOM-CLEAN\n    #print axioms Pic0.albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData\
  \    -> [propext, sorryAx, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]\nSame statement; the sole\
  \ difference is whether the target group object is Pic0.jacobianScheme C or an arbitrary\
  \ abelian variety. So the entire sorryAx residue of the Pic0 form is the PICARD\
  \ REPRESENTABILITY SEAM upstream of this leg, and none of it is Milne's argument.\
  \ Re-runnable by a later session in one command.\n\nDISCHARGED UNCONDITIONALLY THIS\
  \ RUN (Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean, on the project's four-instance abelian-variety\
  \ package): commutativity of an abelian variety (Milne I.1.4) and pointed rigidity\
  \ (Milne I.1.2). A previous session had recorded these as unavailable; the obstruction\
  \ was instance KEYING through the monoidal notation -- (A (x) A).hom is reducibly\
  \ pullback.fst A.hom A.hom >> A.hom -- not missing mathematics.\n\nREMAINING INPUTS:\
  \ (1) SymPowData C (genus C) -- see AJC.albanese.symmetric; (2) Milne III.5.1(a)\
  \ birationality as a SECTION of f^(g) over a dense open. The descent around them\
  \ is closed: extend_to_av (Milne Thm 3.2) is unconditional and axiom-clean, and\
  \ exists_unique_descent_of_section / hom_ext_of_dense_open package it in elementary\
  \ terms with no rational map in the statement.\n\nNOT A CLOSED RESULT ABOUT THE\
  \ JACOBIAN, and the module headers say so in those words. The pinned Pic0.albanese_universal_property\
  \ still reports sorryAx and its six sorries are UNCHANGED -- they are stated against\
  \ a sorry-BODIED SymmetricPower and are undischargeable as stated, which the AlbaneseUP.lean\
  \ header now records along with a pointer to where the mathematics lives.\n"

10	/-!
11	# Milne III.6.1 with the symmetric power *constructed*, not assumed
12	
13	`Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean` proves the Albanese universal property over the interface
14	`SymPowData` — but takes the interface **as a hypothesis**, together with its symmetry
15	`hproj`. `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` then identifies that pair with a colimit of the
16	permutation action. This file composes the two, so the capstone no longer takes a
17	symmetric-power argument at all.
18	
19	## What changes
20	
21	`exists_unique_albanese_of_scheme_colimits` states Milne III.6.1 with
22	
23	* **no `SymPowData` argument** — the symmetric power is `symPowOfColimit C g`;
24	* **no `hproj` argument** — the symmetry is discharged internally by
25	  `symPowOfColimit_proj_perm`, i.e. by `colimit.w`;
26	* one typeclass hypothesis in their place: `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)`.
27	
28	That hypothesis is the honest residue of the whole leg, and by
29	`hasColimit_permDiagram_iff` it is *equivalent* to what the previous statement assumed —
30	so nothing was strengthened in the trade.
31	
32	**Read the binder precisely, because an earlier draft of this file got it wrong.** It is
33	`HasColimit (permDiagram C g)`: **one** diagram, for **this** curve and **this** `g`, in
34	`Over (Spec k̄)`. It is *not*
35	`HasColimitsOfShape (SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin g))) Scheme` — that says every such diagram
36	over every scheme has a colimit, which is strictly stronger, is *not* what
37	`hasColimit_permDiagram_iff` covers, and is in fact believed **false** at this pin
38	(`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` §6: schemes have no coequalizers in general, and a quotient
39	by an equivalence relation need be only an algebraic space). A hypothesis nobody can satisfy
40	would make this theorem vacuously true at every call site and its "single open obligation"
41	undischargeable in principle. The per-diagram binder is satisfiable — one curve, one `g` —
42	and is exactly the one the equivalence theorem names.
43	
44	## What is still assumed, and why it is not this leg's debt
45	
46	Milne III.5.1(a) birationality of `f^{(g)}`, in the same explicit form
47	`AlbaneseFromData.lean` already used: a section over a dense open, a retraction, dominance,
48	two density facts, and the structure-map compatibility `hover`. Those are hypotheses here
49	too. They are geometry about the *Jacobian*, downstream of the Picard seam, and the
50	`ajc-pic0av` lane owns their inputs.
51	
52	## References
53	
54	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.6 Proposition 6.1, p. 104; §III.5 Theorem 5.1(a), p. 101.
55	Blueprint `thm:albanese_universal_property`.
56	-/

22	
23	* **no `SymPowData` argument** — the symmetric power is `symPowOfColimit C g`;
24	* **no `hproj` argument** — the symmetry is discharged internally by
25	  `symPowOfColimit_proj_perm`, i.e. by `colimit.w`;

27

29	`hasColimit_permDiagram_iff` it is *equivalent* to what the previous statement assumed —
30	so nothing was strengthened in the trade.
31	
32	**Read the binder precisely, because an earlier draft of this file got it wrong.** It is
33	`HasColimit (permDiagram C g)`: **one** diagram, for **this** curve and **this** `g`, in
34	`Over (Spec k̄)`. It is *not*
35	`HasColimitsOfShape (SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin g))) Scheme` — that says every such diagram
36	over every scheme has a colimit, which is strictly stronger, is *not* what

name: horizon-inbox
description: Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create; per-team ownership and read-state; and message other projects or teams via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
---

The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and
future), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files
by hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or
fields.

## Read

- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
- In an agent session, an unqualified list means the **open working queue**, not
  archived history. It is ordered by attention: required protections first,
  unread/direct conversations next, then advisory items. JSON starts with an
  `attention` summary so redirecting stderr cannot erase this signal.
- `horizon inbox show <id> --json` opens exactly one item and marks it read for
  your team. Use `--no-mark-read` for inspection without acknowledgement.
- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is
  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale
  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because
  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an
  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.
- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which
  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for
  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:
  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids
  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is
  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.
- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,
  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /
  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience). A conversation
  may have several recipients; start one with `horizon inbox dm <recipient>...`.
  Scope/project says what the item is about.
- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, items addressed
  to its project, and DMs addressed to its own task/run. It should ignore other
  projects' and other teams' addressed items.
- A conversation's participants are its recipients **and its initiator**. The
  initiator is recorded as `metadata.started_by`; replies become unread for every
  other participant, including that initiator. Participants are not ownership:
  the initiator remains responsible for deciding when the thread is finished.
- Kinds: `conversation` (a direct/group thread requiring prompt acknowledgement),
  `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),
  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the
  human — something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project
  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),
  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).

## Ownership & read-state (your team's inbox)

Each running session is a **team**, and the inbox is shared across teams. Two
lightweight overlays keep it navigable:

- **Ownership** — an item is either *shared with everyone* (the default) or
  *owned by one task* (that team's private inbox — e.g. its own memory). Read your
  team's inbox with `horizon inbox list --mine` (owned-by-you **plus** shared);
  another team's private items don't appear. Own an item to your task with
  `horizon inbox add --mine …` (or `--owner <task-id>`), and `horizon inbox own
  <id> --mine|--owner <task>|--shared` to move an existing one. Owning your
  `--kind memory` notes keeps another team's memory out of your working set.
- **Read-state** — read/unread is **per team**, so a shared item several teams see
  tracks who has read it. `horizon inbox list --unread` is what *you* have not read
  yet; `horizon inbox read <id>` marks it read, and `horizon inbox unread <id>`
  puts it back (e.g. you read it but it still needs action). Combine:
  `horizon inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue — the same signal
  the pre-command synchronizer counts for you.

Read in this order before editing:

1. `horizon inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json` — every
   active protection is required even if your team previously marked it read.
2. `horizon inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json` — open each
   result with `inbox show`; reply when a response is needed, otherwise the read
   acknowledgement clears it until another participant replies.
3. Consult hint/issue/info/memory items as advisory context for the task.

The reader/owner id is inferred from your session (your task), so you rarely pass
it explicitly.

## Act

Authorship is automatic: every item and comment you create through the CLI is
attributed to your role (normally `horizon`) from the run environment — you do
**not** pass `--author` (a stray `--author work-reviewer` is demoted to the
`agent` metadata, not used as the author, so the author set stays conventional).
If you are a dispatched **subagent**, add `--agent <your-name>` (e.g. `--agent
work-reviewer`) to record your identity; it is stored in metadata and shown
next to the role in the UI, keeping the author itself a clean role. Items and
comments are also auto-tagged with the run/session provenance (a small chip in the
UI); you do not pass this yourself.

New inbox items use a two-part body:

- First paragraph = concise title. Keep it short enough to scan in one UI row
  (aim for under ~100 characters); do not put the full explanation here.
- Second paragraph and later = non-empty description. Put the evidence, impact,
  next action, and relevant ids/files here. The description is **mandatory** — an
  item that is only a title is rejected.

Write bodies and comments in **Markdown**: the dashboard renders it. Use short
paragraphs and `-` bullet lists instead of one wall-of-text paragraph, `**bold**`
for the key claim, and backticks for ids, lemma names, files, and code
(`` `lem:foo` ``, `` `Foo.lean:42` ``). For a multi-part result, start with a
one-sentence conclusion, then use `## Result`, `## Evidence`, `## Impact`, and
`## Next action` as applicable; omit empty sections. The CLI rejects long new
agent descriptions, opening messages, and comments with no paragraph, heading,
or list structure.

Do not create an item whose body is only a title. If you need a `[persistent]` or
`[temporary]` tag, put it at the start of the title paragraph and keep the rest
of that paragraph concise.

Before opening a new item, search the open inbox for the same topic using
`horizon inbox list --status open --query "key words" --json` and, when relevant,
`--project P` / `--to R`. If a live item already covers the same issue, do not
open a duplicate: add a comment with the new evidence, or edit the body if the
main description is stale. If you discover an open item is obsolete, already
solved, consumed, or superseded, add a short comment when the reason is not
obvious and then run `horizon inbox archive <id>`.

### Conversation lifecycle

A conversation is for an expected reply, decision, or active coordination. A
one-way handoff or announcement is an `info`/`hint`, not a conversation.

1. **Search before starting:** inspect open conversations for the same topic and
   participants (`inbox list --status open --kind conversation --query "key words"
   --json`). Reply to the existing thread whenever it can carry the update. Do not
   open one thread per incremental finding.
2. **One question, one thread:** keep follow-ups, answers, corrections, and the
   final decision as comments on that thread. Start another only when it has a
   genuinely different decision boundary or participant set.
3. **Answer before branching:** when a conversation becomes unread, open it and
   answer or acknowledge it before starting another conversation with the same
   team.
4. **The initiator closes:** if `metadata.started_by` is your task/run, you own
   the lifecycle. Once the requested answer has arrived and been consumed, add a
   short conclusion comment when the outcome is not obvious, then
   `horizon inbox archive <id>`. Do this during the session, not only after a
   warning says the inbox is full.
5. **Do not hide an answer from its initiator:** recipients normally reply and
   leave closure to the initiator. For a human-started thread, answer it but leave
   it open for the human to consume/archive unless the human explicitly delegates
   closure. Use `complete` instead of `archive` only when the concluded thread is
   intentionally meant to remain visible in the resolved working record.

10	/-!
11	# Milne III.6.1 with the symmetric power *constructed*, not assumed
12	
13	`Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean` proves the Albanese universal property over the interface
14	`SymPowData` — but takes the interface **as a hypothesis**, together with its symmetry
15	`hproj`. `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` then identifies that pair with a colimit of the
16	permutation action. This file composes the two, so the capstone no longer takes a
17	symmetric-power argument at all.
18	
19	## What changes
20	
21	`exists_unique_albanese_of_scheme_colimits` states Milne III.6.1 with
22	
23	* **no `SymPowData` argument** — the symmetric power is `symPowOfColimit C g`;
24	* **no `hproj` argument** — the symmetry is discharged internally by
25	  `symPowOfColimit_proj_perm`, i.e. by `colimit.w`;
26	* one typeclass hypothesis in their place: `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)`.
27	
28	That hypothesis is the honest residue of the whole leg, and by
29	`hasColimit_permDiagram_iff` it is *equivalent* to what the previous statement assumed —
30	so nothing was strengthened in the trade.
31	
32	**Read the binder precisely, because an earlier draft of this file got it wrong.** It is
33	`HasColimit (permDiagram C g)`: **one** diagram, for **this** curve and **this** `g`, in
34	`Over (Spec k̄)`. It is *not*
35	`HasColimitsOfShape (SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin g))) Scheme` — that says every such diagram
36	over every scheme has a colimit, which is strictly stronger, is *not* what
37	`hasColimit_permDiagram_iff` covers, and is in fact believed **false** at this pin
38	(`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` §6: schemes have no coequalizers in general, and a quotient
39	by an equivalence relation need be only an algebraic space). A hypothesis nobody can satisfy
40	would make this theorem vacuously true at every call site and its "single open obligation"
41	undischargeable in principle. The per-diagram binder is satisfiable — one curve, one `g` —
42	and is exactly the one the equivalence theorem names.
43	
44	## What is still assumed, and why it is not this leg's debt
45	
46	Milne III.5.1(a) birationality of `f^{(g)}`, in the same explicit form
47	`AlbaneseFromData.lean` already used: a section over a dense open, a retraction, dominance,
48	two density facts, and the structure-map compatibility `hover`. Those are hypotheses here
49	too. They are geometry about the *Jacobian*, downstream of the Picard seam, and the
50	`ajc-pic0av` lane owns their inputs.
51	
52	## References
53	
54	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.6 Proposition 6.1, p. 104; §III.5 Theorem 5.1(a), p. 101.
55	Blueprint `thm:albanese_universal_property`.
